claim: Human patients carrying PAPP-A2 inactivating mutations have low bone mineral density.
source: Human patients carrying PAPP‐A2 inactivating mutations have low bone mineral density.
evidence: Supported by citations to clinical studies (Dauber et al., 2016; Fujimoto et al., 2017) mentioned in the Introduction.

claim: Papp-aa regulates bone calcification by promoting Ca2+-transporting epithelial cell (ionocyte) quiescence-proliferation transition.
source: Using a zebrafish model, we report that Papp-aa regulates bone calcification by promoting Ca2+-transporting epithelial cell (ionocyte) quiescence-proliferation transition.
evidence: Supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing genetic deletion effects and bone calcification measurements.

claim: Ionocytes, which are normally quiescent, re-enter the cell cycle under low [Ca2+] stress.
source: Ionocytes, which are normally quiescent, re-enter the cell cycle under low [Ca2+] stress.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing ionocyte proliferation under low calcium conditions.

claim: Genetic deletion of Papp-aa, but not the closely related Papp-ab, abolished ionocyte proliferation and reduced calcified bone mass.
source: Genetic deletion of Papp-aa, but not the closely related Papp-ab, abolished ionocyte proliferation and reduced calcified bone mass.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from genetic deletion studies shown in Figures 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Loss of Papp-aa expression or activity resulted in diminished IGF1 receptor-Akt-Tor signaling in ionocytes.
source: Loss of Papp-aa expression or activity resulted in diminished IGF1 receptor-Akt-Tor signaling in ionocytes.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing reduced phospho-Akt and phospho-S6 levels in papp-aa mutants (Figure 5).

claim: Under low Ca2+ stress, Papp-aa cleaved Igfbp5a.
source: Under low Ca2+ stress, Papp-aa cleaved Igfbp5a.
evidence: Supported by in vitro proteinase assays and genetic experiments showing calcium-dependent effects.

claim: Under normal conditions, Papp-aa proteinase activity was suppressed and IGFs were sequestered in the IGF/Igfbp complex.
source: Under normal conditions, however, Papp-aa proteinase activity was suppressed and IGFs were sequestered in the IGF/Igfbp complex.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing no effect of Papp-aa deletion under normal calcium conditions and NBI-31772 experiments.

claim: Pharmacological disruption of the IGF/Igfbp complex or adding free IGF1 activated IGF signaling and promoted ionocyte proliferation.
source: Pharmacological disruption of the IGF/Igfbp complex or adding free IGF1 activated IGF signaling and promoted ionocyte proliferation.
evidence: Supported by experimental data using NBI-31772 and IGF1 treatment (Figure 6).

claim: Papp-aa-mediated local Igfbp5a cleavage functions as a [Ca2+]-regulated molecular switch linking IGF signaling to bone calcification by stimulating epithelial cell quiescence-proliferation transition under low Ca2+ stress.
source: These findings suggest that Papp-aa-mediated local Igfbp5a cleavage functions as a [Ca2+]-regulated molecular switch linking IGF signaling to bone calcification by stimulating epithelial cell quiescence-proliferation transition under low Ca2+ stress.
evidence: Supported by integration of multiple experimental findings including genetic, biochemical, and pharmacological data.

claim: PAPP-A and PAPP-A2 belong to the conserved pappalysin proteinase family.
source: Pregnancy-associated plasma protein-a (PAPP‐A) and PAPP‐A2 belong to the conserved pappalysin proteinase family (Boldt et al., 2001; Oxvig, 2015; Conover and Oxvig, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: PAPP-A and PAPP-A2 are zinc metalloproteinases cleaving insulin-like growth factor binding proteins (IGFBPs).
source: Decades of studies suggest that PAPP-A and PAPP-A2 are zinc metalloproteinases cleaving insulin-like growth factor binding proteins (IGFBPs) (Laursen et al., 2007; Oxvig, 2015; Conover and Oxvig, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: IGFBPs are a family of six secreted proteins that bind IGF ligands with high affinity and regulate IGF availability to the IGF1 receptor.
source: IGFBPs are a family of six secreted proteins that bind IGF ligands with high affinity and regulate IGF availability to the IGF1 receptor (Baxter, 2014; Allard and Duan, 2018; Clemmons, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: PAPP-A is tethered to the cell-surface and primarily cleaves IGFBP4 and IGFBP5 among the six IGFBPs.
source: In vitro studies suggested that PAPP-A is tethered to the cell-surface and primarily cleaves IGFBP4 and IGFBP5 among the six IGFBPs.
evidence: Supported by citations to in vitro studies.

claim: PAPP-A2 is secreted and cleaves IGFBP3 and IGFBP5.
source: PAPP-A2, on the other hand, is secreted and cleaves IGFBP3 and IGFBP5 (Oxvig, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Papp-a knockout mice showed a 40% reduction in body size.
source: Papp-a knockout mice showed a 40% reduction in body size (Conover et al., 2004), a phenotype similar to those of the IGF1 and IGF2 mutant mice (Baker et al., 1993; Liu et al., 1993).
evidence: Supported by citations to published mouse studies.

claim: Papp-a2 knockout mice had a modest decrease in body size.
source: Papp-a2 knockout mice had a modest decrease in body size (Christians et al., 2013; Christians et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to published mouse studies.

claim: Human patients carrying inactivating mutations in the PAPP-A2 gene displayed progressive growth failure.
source: This notion is further supported by recent clinical studies showing that human patients carrying inactivating mutations in the PAPP-A2 gene displayed progressive growth failure (Dauber et al., 2016; Fujimoto et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: Human patients with PAPP-A2 mutations had lower bone mineral density.
source: In addition to reduced body height, these patients also had lower bone mineral density (Dauber et al., 2016; Fujimoto et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: Papp-a mutant mice had delayed appearance of ossification centers and reduced calcified bone mass.
source: Likewise, the Papp-a mutant mice had delayed appearance of ossification centers and reduced calcified bone mass (Conover et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to published mouse study.

claim: Papp-a2 mutant mice had sex-and age-specific defects in bone structure and mineral density.
source: The Papp-a2 mutant mice had sex-and age-specific defects in bone structure and mineral density (Christians et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to published mouse study.

claim: Genetic deletion of IGF binding protein 5a (Igfbp5a) results in reduced calcified bone mass in zebrafish even though igfbp5a is not expressed in skeletal tissues.
source: We have recently found that genetic deletion of IGF binding protein 5a (Igfbp5a), a major PAPP-A substrate, results in reduced calcified bone mass in zebrafish even though igfbp5a is not expressed in skeletal tissues (Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study by the authors.

claim: In zebrafish embryos and larvae, igfbp5a is specifically expressed in a population of Ca2+-transporting epithelial cells (ionocytes) located in the yolk sac.
source: In zebrafish embryos and larvae, igfbp5a is specifically expressed in a population of Ca2+-transporting epithelial cells (ionocytes) located in the yolk sac (Dai et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: NaR cells are functionally similar to human intestinal epithelial cells.
source: These ionocytes, known as NaR cells, are functionally similar to human intestinal epithelial cells.
evidence: Based on functional comparison and established knowledge.

claim: NaR cells play a key role in maintaining body Ca2+ homeostasis by uptaking Ca2+ from the surrounding habitat.
source: They play a key role in maintaining body Ca2+ homeostasis by uptaking Ca2+ from the surrounding habitat, (Hwang, 2009; Lin and Hwang, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: A hallmark of NaR cells and human intestinal epithelial cells is the expression of Trpv6/TRPV6, a constitutive calcium channel constituting the first and rate-limiting step in the transcellular Ca2+ transport pathway.
source: A hallmark of NaR cells and human intestinal epithelial cells is the expression of Trpv6/TRPV6, a constitutive calcium channel constituting the first and rate-limiting step in the transcellular Ca2+ transport pathway (Hoenderop et al., 2005; Pan et al., 2005; Dai et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Trpv6/TRPV6 regulates NaR cell quiescence.
source: Trpv6/TRPV6 also regulates NaR cell quiescence (Xin et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to published study.

claim: NaR cells, normally non-dividing and quiescent, rapidly exit quiescence and re-enter the cell cycle in response to low [Ca2+] stress.
source: NaR cells, normally non-dividing and quiescent, rapidly exit quiescence and re-enter the cell cycle in response to low [Ca2+] stress (Dai et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to published studies.

claim: NaR cell reactivation in response to low calcium is an adaptive response allowing animals to take up adequate Ca2+ for maintaining body Ca2+ homeostasis and survive under low [Ca2+] conditions.
source: This is thought to be an adaptive response, allowing animals to take up adequate Ca2+ for maintaining body Ca2+ homeostasis and survive under low [Ca2+] conditions (Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation and inference about adaptive function.

claim: The lower [Ca2+] stress-induced adaptive NaR cell reactivation and proliferation were impaired in igfbp5a-/- fish.
source: Interestingly, while no change was observed in NaR cells under normal [Ca2+] conditions, the lower [Ca2+] stress-induced adaptive NaR cell reactivation and proliferation were impaired in igfbp5a-/- fish (Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Zebrafish have three genes belonging to the pappalysin family, including papp-aa, papp-ab, and papp-a2.
source: Zebrafish have three genes belonging to the pappalysin family, including papp-aa, papp-ab, and papp-a2 (Kjaer-Sorensen et al., 2013; Kjaer-Sorensen et al., 2014; Wolman et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: papp-aa is highly expressed in NaR cells.
source: among the three genes, papp-aa is highly expressed in NaR cells.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from FACS and qPCR analysis shown in Figure 1.

claim: The mRNA levels of papp-aa in NaR cells were 2-fold higher than those of papp-ab and papp-a2.
source: The mRNA levels of papp-aa in NaR cells were 2-fold higher than those of papp-ab and papp-a2 (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Low [Ca2+] stress treatment had no effect on papp-aa, papp-ab, or papp-a2 mRNA levels.
source: Low [Ca2+] stress treatment had no effect on their mRNA levels (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The level of papp-aa mRNA in NaR cells was approximately 10-fold greater than in non-GFP cells from the rest of the fish body.
source: The level of papp-aa mRNA in NaR cells was approximately 10-fold greater (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The papp-ab mRNA levels were similar between NaR cells and other cells.
source: In comparison, the papp-ab mRNA levels were similar between NaR cells and other cells (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: papp-aa mRNA signals were detected in cells in the yolk sac region beginning at three dpf.
source: Meanwhile, papp-aa mRNA signals were detected in cells in the yolk sac region beginning at three dpf (Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: papp-aa mRNA was expressed in NaR cells.
source: Double color label staining showed that papp-aa mRNA was indeed expressed in NaR cells (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by double-label staining data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Under the normal [Ca2+] condition, NaR cell numbers between wild-type, heterozygous, and papp-aa-/- mutant fish were similar.
source: Under the normal [Ca2+] condition, NaR cell numbers between these three different genotype groups were similar (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: Low [Ca2+] stress treatment resulted in a 4-fold, highly significant increase in NaR cell number in the wild-type and heterozygous fish groups.
source: Low [Ca2+] stress treatment, however, resulted in a 4-fold, highly significant increase in NaR cell number in the wild-type and heterozygous fish groups.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: The low calcium-induced increase in NaR cell number was abolished in papp-aa-/- mutant fish.
source: This increase was abolished in papp-aa-/- mutant fish (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: Deletion of Papp-ab had no effect on low [Ca2+] stress-induced NaR cell increase nor did it affect NaR cell number under the normal [Ca2+] condition.
source: Deletion of Papp-ab had no effect on low [Ca2+] stress-induced NaR cell increase nor did it affect NaR cell number under the normal [Ca2+] condition (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: NaR cell re-activation was abolished in papp-aa-/-;Tg(igfbp5a:GFP) larvae under low calcium stress.
source: While NaR cells in papp-aa+/+;Tg(igfbp5a:GFP) larvae and papp-aa+/-;Tg(igfbp5a:GFP) larvae divided robustly under low [Ca2+] stress, NaR cell re-activation was abolished in papp-aa-/-;Tg(igfbp5a:GFP) larvae (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: Deletion of Papp-aa did not change HR or NCC cell numbers.
source: Deletion of Papp-aa did not change HR or NCC cell numbers (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: No difference was observed between papp-aa-/- mutant fish and their siblings in terms of gross appearance, growth rate, or developmental speed.
source: No difference was observed between papp-aa-/- mutant fish and their siblings in terms of gross appearance, growth rate, or developmental speed (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–E.

claim: NaR cells in wild-type Tg(igfbp5a:GFP) larvae had a narrow apical opening when kept in the normal [Ca2+] medium.
source: We noted that NaR cells in wild-type Tg(igfbp5a:GFP) larvae had a narrow apical opening when kept in the normal [Ca2+] medium (Figure 2—figure supplement 3F).
evidence: Supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3F.

claim: The apical opening of NaR cells became markedly enlarged under low [Ca2+] stress treatment.
source: This apical opening became markedly enlarged under low [Ca2+] stress treatment (Figure 2—figure supplement 3F).
evidence: Supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3F.

claim: The low [Ca2+] stress-induced morphological change in NaR was absent in papp-aa-/- mutant fish.
source: Although the functional significance of this morphological change is unclear, this low [Ca2+] stress-induced morphological change in NaR was absent in papp-aa-/- mutant fish (Figure 2—figure supplement 3F).
evidence: Supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3F.

claim: There was a complete lack of calcified bone in papp-aa-/- fish at seven dpf.
source: Alizarin red staining analysis indicated a complete lack of calcified bone in papp-aa-/- fish at seven dpf (Figure 2F).
evidence: Supported by Alizarin red staining data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: At 10 and 12 dpf, some components of the craniofacial skeleton in papp-aa-/- fish were calcified, albeit at very low levels.
source: At 10 and 12 dpf, some components of the craniofacial skeleton in papp-aa-/- fish were calcified, albeit at very low levels (Figure 2G; Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by Alizarin red staining data shown in Figure 2G and Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: None of the vertebral columns in papp-aa-/- fish were stained by Alizarin red even at 10 and 12 dpf.
source: However, none of the vertebral columns in papp-aa-/- fish were stained by Alizarin red even at 10 and 12 dpf, suggesting the mutant fish suffered from Ca2+ deficiency (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by Alizarin red staining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: papp-aa-/- mutant fish died around 2 weeks when kept under normal [Ca2+].
source: In agreement with a previous report (Wolman et al., 2015), papp-aa-/- mutant fish died around 2 weeks when kept under normal [Ca2+].
evidence: Supported by observation and citation to previous report.

claim: Re-introduction of Papp-aa restored low [Ca2+] stress-induced NaR cell reactivation in papp-aa-/-; Tg(igfbp5a:GFP) fish.
source: Re-introduction of Papp-aa restored low [Ca2+] stress-induced NaR cell reactivation (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: Supported by genetic mosaic assay data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Papp-aa cleaved Igfbp5a, while Papp-aa E501A had little proteolytic activity.
source: As expected, while Papp-aa cleaved Igfbp5a, Papp-aa E501A had little proteolytic activity (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by in vitro proteinase assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The E501A mutant of Papp-aa had no effect in rescuing NaR cell reactivation when expressed in NaR cells in papp-aa-/-; Tg(igfbp5a:GFP).
source: When the E501A mutant was expressed in NaR cells in papp-aa-/-; Tg(igfbp5a:GFP) using the genetic mosaic assay, it had no effect in rescuing NaR cell reactivation (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: Supported by genetic mosaic assay data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: ZnCl2 inhibited low [Ca2+] stress-induced NaR cell proliferation.
source: Both compounds inhibited low [Ca2+] stress-induced NaR cell proliferation (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: Supported by drug treatment data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Batimastat inhibited low [Ca2+] stress-induced NaR cell proliferation.
source: Both compounds inhibited low [Ca2+] stress-induced NaR cell proliferation (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: Supported by drug treatment data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Targeted expression of STC1 in NaR cells inhibited low [Ca2+] stress-induced NaR cell proliferation.
source: When STC1 was specifically expressed in a subset of NaR cells using the genetic mosaic assay, it inhibited low [Ca2+] stress-induced NaR cell proliferation, while mCherry expression had no such effect (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: Supported by genetic mosaic assay data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: Targeted expression of STC2 inhibited low [Ca2+] stress-induced NaR cell proliferation.
source: Likewise, targeted expression of STC2 also inhibited low [Ca2+] stress-induced NaR cell proliferation (Figure 3H).
evidence: Supported by genetic mosaic assay data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Papp-aa containing medium efficiently cleaved IGFBP5 and IGFBP4.
source: As shown in Figure 4A, Papp-aa containing medium efficiently cleaved IGFBP5 and IGFBP4, whereas it did not cleave IGFBP1, 2, 3 and 6 (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by in vitro proteinase assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Papp-aa did not cleave IGFBP1, 2, 3 and 6.
source: As shown in Figure 4A, Papp-aa containing medium efficiently cleaved IGFBP5 and IGFBP4, whereas it did not cleave IGFBP1, 2, 3 and 6 (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by in vitro proteinase assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Both zebrafish Papp-aa and Papp-ab cleaved Igfbp5a, whereas Papp-a2 had little activity.
source: Both zebrafish Papp-aa and Papp-ab cleaved Igfbp5a, whereas Papp-a2 had little activity (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by in vitro proteinase assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Igfbp5b was cleaved by Papp-aa, Papp-ab, and Papp-a2.
source: In the case of Igfbp5b, it was cleaved by Papp-aa, Papp-ab, and Papp-a2 (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by in vitro proteinase assay data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Changing Igfbp5a K148 to alanine reduced Papp-aa-mediated cleavage, while mutating the neighboring K147 had little effect.
source: Indeed, changing Igfbp5a K148 to alanine reduced Papp-aa-mediated cleavage, while mutating the neighboring K147 had little effect (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by in vitro proteinase assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Changing Igfbp5b K145 to alanine reduced Papp-aa-mediated Igfbp5b cleavage, while K144A mutation had little effect.
source: Likewise, changing Igfbp5b K145 to alanine reduced Papp-aa-mediated Igfbp5b cleavage, while K144A mutation had little effect (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by in vitro proteinase assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Papp-aa and Papp-ab did not cleave Igfbp3 and Papp-a2 had very low activity.
source: Papp-aa and Papp-ab did not cleave Igfbp3 and Papp-a2 had very low activity (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by in vitro proteinase assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Igfbp5a and Igfbp2a are highly expressed in NaR cells.
source: Gene expression analysis results showed that Igfbp5a and Igfbp2a are highly expressed in NaR cells (Figure 4D).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The levels of igfbp5b, igfbp1b, igfbp3, and igfbp6b mRNA in NaR cells are much lower, and igfbp2b and igfbp6a are barely detectable.
source: The levels of igfbp5b, igfbp1b, igfbp3, and igfbp6b mRNA in NaR cells are much lower, and igfbp2b and igfbp6a are barely detectable (Figure 4D).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Low [Ca2+] stress treatment did not affect igfbp mRNA levels.
source: Low [Ca2+] stress treatment did not affect any of these igfbp mRNA levels (Figure 4D).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Under normal [Ca2+] conditions, NaR cell numbers in papp-aa-/- fish, igfbp5a-/- fish, papp-aa-/-;igfbp5a-/- double mutant fish, and siblings were similar and no significant difference was observed.
source: As shown in Figure 4E, under normal [Ca2+] conditions, NaR cell numbers in papp-aa-/- fish, igfbp5a-/- fish, papp-aa-/-;igfbp5a-/- double mutant fish, and siblings were similar and no significant difference was observed (Figure 4E).
evidence: Supported by genetic analysis data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The low [Ca2+] stress-induced increase in NaR cell number was abolished in papp-aa-/- fish, igfbp5a-/- fish, and papp-aa-/-;igfbp5a-/- double mutant fish.
source: While the low [Ca2+] stress treatment resulted in a significant increase in NaR cell number in the siblings, this increase was abolished in papp-aa-/- fish, igfbp5a-/- fish, and papp-aa-/-;igfbp5a-/- double mutant fish (Figure 4E).
evidence: Supported by genetic analysis data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Low [Ca2+] stress treatment activates Akt and Tor activity in wild-type fish NaR cells.
source: As previously reported (Dai et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2018), low [Ca2+] stress treatment activates Akt and Tor activity in wild-type fish NaR cells (Figure 5A and B; Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5A, B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, and citations to previous reports.

claim: The low [Ca2+] stress-induced Akt and Tor signaling was impaired in papp-aa-/- fish but not in the heterozygous fish.
source: This induction was impaired in papp-aa-/- fish but not in the heterozygous fish (Figure 5A and B; Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5A, B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Treatment of wild-type zebrafish larvae with ZnCl2 and batimastat inhibited the low [Ca2+] stress-induced Akt and Tor activity.
source: Treatment of wild-type zebrafish larvae with ZnCl2 and batimastat also inhibited the low [Ca2+] stress-induced Akt and Tor activity (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: Supported by drug treatment and immunostaining data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Targeted expression of myr-Akt restored NaR cell reactivation in papp-aa-/- fish under low [Ca2+] stress.
source: Indeed, genetic mosaic assays showed that targeted expression of myr-Akt, a constitutively active Akt (Kohn et al., 1996), restored NaR cell reactivation in papp-aa-/- fish under to low [Ca2+] stress (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: Supported by genetic mosaic assay data shown in Figure 5E and F.

claim: NBI-31772 treatment promoted NaR cell reactivation under normal [Ca2+] in a concentration-dependent manner.
source: NBI-31772 treatment promoted NaR cell reactivation under normal [Ca2+] in a concentration-dependent manner (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: Supported by drug treatment data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: NBI-31772 treatment increased Akt and Tor signaling activity.
source: While NBI-31772 treatment increased Akt and Tor signaling activity, these increases were abolished by BMS-754807 (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: The increases in Akt and Tor signaling activity induced by NBI-31772 were abolished by BMS-754807.
source: While NBI-31772 treatment increased Akt and Tor signaling activity, these increases were abolished by BMS-754807 (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: The effect of NBI-31772 in reactivating NaR cells was abolished by adding BMS-754807, PI3 kinase inhibitor wortmannin, Akt inhibitor MK2260, and Tor inhibitor rapamycin.
source: Moreover, the effect of NBI-31772 in reactivating NaR cells was abolished by adding BMS-754807, PI3 kinase inhibitor wortmannin, Akt inhibitor MK2260, and Tor inhibitor rapamycin (Figure 6E; Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by drug treatment data shown in Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: NBI-31772 treatment did not change the phospho-Erk levels.
source: Immunostaining analysis results showed that NBI-31772 treatment did not change the phospho-Erk levels (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Co-treatment with the MEK inhibitor U0260 did not affect NBI-31772 treatment-induced NaR cell proliferation.
source: Co-treatment with the MEK inhibitor U0260 did not affect NBI-31772 treatment-induced NaR cell proliferation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), indicating MAPK signaling is not involved.
evidence: Supported by drug treatment data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Addition of human IGF1 significantly increased NaR cell reactivation and proliferation under normal [Ca2+].
source: As shown in Figure 6F, IGF1 treatment significantly increased NaR cell reactivation and proliferation under normal [Ca2+].
evidence: Supported by IGF1 treatment data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Fish (salmon) IGF1 treatment increased NaR cell reactivation and proliferation under normal [Ca2+] conditions.
source: Likewise, fish (salmon) IGF1 treatment also increased NaR cell reactivation and proliferation under normal [Ca2+] conditions (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by IGF1 treatment data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Zebrafish shares many similarities in bone biology with mammals, including bone formation, resorption, mineralization, and extracellular matrix maintenance.
source: Zebrafish shares many similarities in bone biology with mammals, including bone formation, resorption, mineralization, and extracellular matrix maintenance (Laizé et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Unlike mammals, zebrafish bone is acellular and osteoclasts are mononucleated.
source: Unlike mammals, however, zebrafish bone is acellular and osteoclasts are mononucleated (Laizé et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Many hormones known to be critical to mammalian bone mineralization, including Vitamin D3, parathyroid hormone, calcitonin were found to be important in zebrafish.
source: Many hormones known to be critical to mammalian bone mineralization, including Vitamin D3, parathyroid hormone, calcitonin were found to be important in zebrafish (Lin and Hwang, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Stanniocalcin (Stc) was initially discovered in bony fish as a hypocalcemic hormone.
source: Stanniocalcin (Stc), for example, was initially discovered in bony fish as a hypocalcemic hormone (Pang, 1973).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Humans and other mammals have two STC genes.
source: It was later found that humans and other mammals have two STC genes (Yeung et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Human STC1 and STC2 are potent PAPP-A and A2 inhibitors in vitro.
source: Recent studies suggest that human STC1 and STC2 are potent PAPP-A and A2 inhibitors in vitro (Jepsen et al., 2015; Kløverpris et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Papp-aa acts by cleaving Igfbp5a and activating IGF1 receptor-mediated Akt and Tor signaling in NaR cells in response to low [Ca2+] stress.
source: Mechanistically, Papp-aa acts by cleaving Igfbp5a and activating IGF1 receptor-mediated Akt and Tor signaling in NaR cells in response to low [Ca2+] stress.
evidence: Supported by integration of multiple experimental findings.

claim: Papp-aa-mediated Igfbp5a proteolysis in NaR cells is suppressed under normal [Ca2+] conditions.
source: A most interesting finding made in this study is that Papp-aa-mediated Igfbp5a proteolysis in NaR cells is suppressed under normal [Ca2+] conditions.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing calcium-dependent effects.

claim: Genetic deletion of Papp-aa had no effect on Akt-Tor signaling or NaR cell proliferation when fish were kept under normal [Ca2+] conditions.
source: This conclusion is supported by the fact that genetic deletion of Papp-aa had no effect on Akt-Tor signaling or NaR cell proliferation when fish were kept under normal [Ca2+] conditions, while it abolished IGF signaling and NaR cell reactivation and proliferation under low [Ca2+] stress.
evidence: Supported by experimental data comparing normal and low calcium conditions.

claim: Papp-aa-mediated Igfbp5a proteolysis functions as a [Ca2+]-regulated molecular switch to turn on and off IGF signaling in NaR cells.
source: The data presented in this study suggests that Papp-aa-mediated Igfbp5a proteolysis functions as a [Ca2+]-regulated molecular switch to turn on and off IGF signaling in NaR cells.
evidence: Supported by integration of multiple experimental findings and mechanistic interpretation.

claim: Under normal conditions, Papp-aa activity is suppressed at low levels and Igfbp5a is intact.
source: Under normal conditions, Papp-aa activity is suppressed at low levels and Igfbp5a is intact.
evidence: Inferred from experimental data showing calcium-dependent effects.

claim: Intact Igfbp5a acts as an IGF inhibitory protein as it binds IGF ligands and prevents its binding and activation of the IGF1 receptor.
source: Intact Igfbp5a acts as an IGF inhibitory protein as it binds IGF ligands and prevents its binding and activation of the IGF1 receptor.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of IGFBP function and experimental data.

claim: Under low [Ca2+] stress, Papp-a activity is increased.
source: Under low [Ca2+] stress, Papp-a activity is increased.
evidence: Inferred from experimental data showing calcium-dependent effects.

claim: Papp-aa proteolytically cleaves Igfbp5a and releases IGFs from the Igfbp5a/IGF complex to activate IGF1 receptor-mediated PI3 kinase-Akt-Tor signaling under low calcium stress.
source: Papp-aa proteolytically cleaves Igfbp5a and releases IGFs from the Igfbp5a/IGF complex to activate IGF1 receptor-mediated PI3 kinase-Akt-Tor signaling, thus promoting NaR cell proliferation (Figure 6G).
evidence: Supported by integration of multiple experimental findings and model shown in Figure 6G.

claim: When Igfbp5a/IGFBP5 is present in a microenvironment containing active Papp-aa, it potentiates IGF action because Papp-aa-mediated Igfbp5a proteolysis releases IGFs from the Igfbp5a/IGF complex.
source: We suggest that when Igfbp5a/IGFBP5 is present in a microenvironment containing active Papp-aa, it potentiates IGF action because Papp-aa-mediated Igfbp5a proteolysis releases IGFs from the Igfbp5a/IGF complex.
evidence: Based on mechanistic interpretation of experimental data.

claim: When Igfbp5/IGFBP5 is expressed in tissues without Papp-aa or with Papp-aa activity inhibited, it inhibits IGF action as Igfbp5a binds to IGFs and sequesters IGFs in the IGF/Igfbp5a complex.
source: When Igfbp5/IGFBP5 is expressed in tissues without Papp-aa or with Papp-aa activity inhibited, it inhibits IGF action as Igfbp5a binds to IGFs and sequesters IGFs in the IGF/Igfbp5a complex.
evidence: Based on mechanistic interpretation of experimental data.

claim: Insulin/IGF-PI3 kinase-Akt-Tor signaling pathway is critical in adult stem cell quiescence regulation.
source: Genetic studies in flies and mice suggest that insulin/IGF-PI3 kinase-Akt-Tor signaling pathway is critical in adult stem cell quiescence regulation (Chen et al., 2009; Ito and Suda, 2014; Ziegler et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: In Drosophila, neural stem cells are reactivated in response to dietary amino acids and this has been attributed to insulin produced in glia cells.
source: In Drosophila, neural stem cells are reactivated in response to dietary amino acids and this has been attributed to insulin produced in glia cells (Chell and Brand, 2010; Sousa-Nunes et al., 2011; Huang and Wang, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Reactivation of the imprinted IGF2 gene expression or activation of mTOR in mouse adult hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) promotes them to exit quiescence and proliferate.
source: Reactivation of the imprinted IGF2 gene expression or activation of mTOR in mouse adult hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) promotes them to exit quiescence and proliferate (Chen et al., 2008; Venkatraman et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: IGF2 stimulates adult neural stem cell and intestinal stem cell reactivation in mice.
source: IGF2 also stimulates adult neural stem cell and intestinal stem cell reactivation in mice (Ferrón et al., 2015; Ziegler et al., 2015; Ziegler et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Elevated PI3 kinase-Akt-Tor activity stimulates reactivation of adult stem cells in Drosophila and mice.
source: Elevated PI3 kinase-Akt-Tor activity stimulates reactivation of adult stem cells in Drosophila and mice (Chell and Brand, 2010; Sousa-Nunes et al., 2011; Gil-Ranedo et al., 2019; Hemmati et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The mechanisms underlying cell type- and cell state-specific activation of insulin/IGF-PI3 kinase-Akt-Tor signaling in reactivating quiescent adult stem cells are poorly understood.
source: Although the role of insulin/IGF-PI3 kinase-Akt-Tor signaling in reactivating quiescent adult stem cells has been demonstrated across a wide range of species, the mechanisms underlying its cell type- and cell state-specific activation are poorly understood.
evidence: Based on review of literature and identification of knowledge gap.

claim: The similarities among mammals, flies, and fish imply evolutionarily conserved and general mechanisms at work.
source: The similarities among mammals, flies, and fish imply evolutionarily conserved and general mechanisms at work.
evidence: Based on comparative analysis across species.

claim: The zebrafish genome does not have an igfbp4 gene.
source: The zebrafish genome has no igfbp4 gene, but contains two paralogous igfbp5 genes (Allard and Duan, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The zebrafish genome contains two paralogous igfbp5 genes.
source: The zebrafish genome has no igfbp4 gene, but contains two paralogous igfbp5 genes (Allard and Duan, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: K128 in human IGFBP5 is critical for PAPP-A-mediated cleavage.
source: K128 in human IGFBP5 is critical for PAPP-A-mediated cleavage (Laursen et al., 2001; Laursen et al., 2002), and this residue is present in zebrafish Igfbp5a (K147 or K148) and Igfbp5b (K144 or K145) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature and sequence alignment shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Human IGFBP5 is degraded by a host of proteinases including thrombin, elastase, cathepsin G, C1s, ADAM 9, ADAM 12 s, MMP-1, and MMP-2.
source: In addition to PAPP-A and -A2, thrombin, elastase, cathepsin G, C1s, ADAM 9, ADAM 12 s, MMP-1, and MMP-2 etc. have been shown to degrade IGFBP5 in vitro (Duan and Allard, 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Changes in external [Ca2+] did not change papp-aa mRNA level nor igfbp5a mRNA level.
source: Since changes in external [Ca2+] did not change papp-aa mRNA level nor igfbp5a mRNA level, and because addition of free IGF1 or pharmacological disruption of the Igfbp/IGF complex was sufficient to activate IGF signaling and induce NaR cell reactivation under normal [Ca2+] conditions, we speculate that there is a [Ca2+]-regulated post-transcriptional mechanism(s) at work.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 4D.

claim: There is a [Ca2+]-regulated post-transcriptional mechanism(s) regulating Papp-aa activity.
source: Since changes in external [Ca2+] did not change papp-aa mRNA level nor igfbp5a mRNA level, and because addition of free IGF1 or pharmacological disruption of the Igfbp/IGF complex was sufficient to activate IGF signaling and induce NaR cell reactivation under normal [Ca2+] conditions, we speculate that there is a [Ca2+]-regulated post-transcriptional mechanism(s) at work.
evidence: Based on inference from experimental data and speculation about mechanism.

claim: Mammalian PAPP-A proteolytic activity is inhibited by STC1 and STC2.
source: Recent studies showed that mammalian PAPP-A proteolytic activity is inhibited by STC1 and STC2 (Jepsen et al., 2015; Kløverpris et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Overexpression of STC1 or STC2 in NaR cells impaired Papp-aa-induced IGF signaling and NaR cell reactivation in vivo.
source: In this study, we showed that overexpression of STC1 or STC2 in NaR cells impaired Papp-aa-induced IGF signaling and NaR cell reactivation in vivo.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F, G, and H.

claim: The zebrafish genome has four stc genes.
source: We now understand that the human genome has two STC genes while the zebrafish genome has four stc genes (Yeung et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The mRNA levels of stc1 but not the other stc genes are significantly higher in fish raised in high [Ca2+] medium compared to those kept in low [Ca2+] medium.
source: The mRNA levels of stc1 but not the other stc genes are significantly higher in fish raised in high [Ca2+] medium compared to those kept in low [Ca2+] medium (Chou et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Forced expression and morpholino-based knockdown of Stc1 altered NaR cell density and Ca2+ uptake.
source: Forced expression and morpholino-based knockdown of Stc1 altered NaR cell density and Ca2+ uptake (Tseng et al., 2009), although these manipulations have also changed HR and NCC cell density and the uptake of other ions (Chou et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Both human PAPP-A and zebrafish Papp-aa contain three Lin-12/Notch repeat (LNR) modules.
source: It is also worth noting that both human PAPP-A and zebrafish Papp-aa contain three Lin-12/Notch repeat (LNR) modules (Boldt et al., 2004; Wolman et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The three LNR modules in human PAPP-A can bind Ca2+ and form a Ca2+-dependent substrate binding exosite.
source: The three LNR modules in human PAPP-A can bind Ca2+ and form a Ca2+-dependent substrate binding exosite (Boldt et al., 2004; Weyer et al., 2007; Mikkelsen et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Reactivation of quiescent cells is critical for tissue repair, regeneration, and adult stem cell renewal.
source: Reactivation of quiescent cells is critical for tissue repair, regeneration, and adult stem cell renewal (Cheung and Rando, 2013; Spencer et al., 2013; Yao, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The low [Ca2+] stress-induced Akt signaling activity was similarly impaired in papp-aa-/- single mutant and papp-aa-/-; igfbp5a-/- double mutant fish.
source: The low [Ca2+] stress-induced Akt signaling activity was similarly impaired in papp-aa-/- single mutant and papp-aa-/-; igfbp5a-/- double mutant fish (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: papp-aa mRNA is expressed in various neural tissues.
source: To date, published whole mount in situ hybridization data suggest that papp-aa mRNA is expressed in various neural tissues, papp-ab mRNA in developing myotomes and brain (Kjaer-Sorensen et al., 2013; Wolman et al., 2015; Miller et al., 2018; Alassaf et al., 2019), and papp-a2 in the notochord and brain (Kjaer-Sorensen et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: papp-ab mRNA is expressed in developing myotomes and brain.
source: To date, published whole mount in situ hybridization data suggest that papp-aa mRNA is expressed in various neural tissues, papp-ab mRNA in developing myotomes and brain (Kjaer-Sorensen et al., 2013; Wolman et al., 2015; Miller et al., 2018; Alassaf et al., 2019), and papp-a2 in the notochord and brain (Kjaer-Sorensen et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: papp-a2 mRNA is expressed in the notochord and brain.
source: To date, published whole mount in situ hybridization data suggest that papp-aa mRNA is expressed in various neural tissues, papp-ab mRNA in developing myotomes and brain (Kjaer-Sorensen et al., 2013; Wolman et al., 2015; Miller et al., 2018; Alassaf et al., 2019), and papp-a2 in the notochord and brain (Kjaer-Sorensen et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Strong papp-aa mRNA signal was detected in the brain.
source: In agreement with previous reports (Wolman et al., 2015), strong papp-aa mRNA signal was detected in the brain (Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1D and citation to previous report.
